title: feat: introduce `html` templating
body:
⚠️ **DO NOT MERGE YET** ## Summary This PR introduces `html` templating in InstantSearch.js. This allows InstantSearch.js users to pass templates as HTML strings safely, with easier access to exposed data, and with an easier API to set up events. [**Read RFC →**](https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch-rfcs/blob/master/accepted/html-templating-instantsearch.md) ```js instantsearch.widgets.hits({ // ... templates: { item(hit, { html, components, sendEvent }) { return html`

${components.Highlight({ hit, attribute: 'name' })}

${components.Snippet({ hit, attribute: 'description' })}

`; }, }, }); ``` ## Review ### Tests **This feature involves many tests in a lot of widgets, along with fixes in a buncg of existing types. To keep the changes digestible, I've added widget-level tests in a separate PR.** ### New components The PR introduces new VDOM components: `Highlight`, `Snippet`, `ReverseHighlight`, and `ReverseSnippet` which are exposed in the templates of the `hits` and `infiniteHits` widgets. They depend on a common implementation from [`ui-components/highlight-vdom`](https://github.com/algolia/ui-components/tree/master/packages/highlight-vdom) and are wrapped internally to add the InstantSearch-specific class names. This wrapping will have to be done in every VDOM-based flavor. In the future, we may want to move those in a separate `instantsearch-vdom` package. The final components exposed in templates live in `src/helpers/components/` (with the logic to parse hits and pass parts to the UI component), near their existing string-based counterparts. ### CI failures Some checks don't pass, notably the type checks for `geoSearch` because the `HTMLMarker` is currently designed to work with plain HTML. I'll fix this in a dedicated PR.
